summary: A hatted village figure - tapering torso, belted tunic, two-joint legs and arms - with a procedural walk cycle whose arms counter-swing the legs and whose torso leans with speed.
objective: Seen from about three metres the figure reads as three tiers of detail: standing person silhouette with a hat and a tunic hem, then jointed limbs, belt, boots and collar, then cuff bands, eye highlights and hem stitching; in motion each arm swings against the leg on its side.
intent_signals: add a villager walking down the lane
example_prompts: Walk two villagers between the market stall and the well.
I need a person-scale figure whose arms swing properly against the legs.
not_for: Anatomy, medical or ergonomic reference of any kind.
A portrait or likeness of any real person.
Skinned deformation, cloth simulation or facial animation.

silhouette: standing figure 1.75 m to the crown, shoulders 0.44 m across tapering to a belted waist
hat crown and brim breaking the head outline, and a tunic hem cutting the thigh line
arms held clear of the body so the gap between arm and torso reads at any distance
in motion: opposite arm and leg lead together, and the torso leans 6 degrees into the walk
medium: two-joint legs and arms - thigh, shin, boot and upper arm, forearm, hand
belt with a buckle, boot soles standing 2.5 cm proud, and a collar at the neck
boots that stay flat through stance and roll over the toe through swing
hip bob of 2.6 cm at twice the stride rate, with a 3 degree hip counter-rotation
fine: cuff band turned at each wrist, 8 mm thick
eyes 3.8 cm across with a 1.2 cm highlight, shaded by the hat brim above them
a nose block on the face, so the head has a front at the detail distance
fourteen hem stitches around the tunic skirt, jittered per seed

principles: Counter-swing is what makes a walk read as a person: the arm opposite the leading leg leads, and the moment both swing together the figure reads as a marching toy.
Lean the torso with speed, not the whole figure: leaning at the hips keeps the feet planted where the gait put them.
Phase advances by distance travelled, not by time, so a villager slowed to half speed takes the same steps more slowly instead of skating.
implementation: Call create({ scale, strideM, strideHz, speed, seed, tunic, yawRateRad }); the group is centred on its footprint with y = 0 at the ground plane and the figure facing +Z.
Call animate(dt) every frame; it returns false for dt <= 0 and true when the pose advanced. animate(dt, speed) overrides the cruise speed from that frame onward.
speed = 0 means cruise, which is strideM x strideHz x scale.
setRoute(points, loop) takes [x, z] or [x, y, z] points - the polyline from layout/village-layout.js drops straight in - and turns at no more than yawRateRad.
Attach a lantern or a basket at the harness socket and a hat at head; back carries a pack.
Sockets are ordered harness, head, back: the proof harness aims its detail view at sockets[0] and lifts that anchor by 0.35 of the figure's height, so the belt socket is what frames the face.
observable_checks: Run scripts/kit-proof.py and count features in close.png: at least two from each detail-ladder band must be visible in the frame.
Step animate(1/60) and compare the z of hand-0 with the z of foot-0: their leads must have opposite signs (kits-creatures.test.js asserts this).
Through each stance run, the world x and z of foot-0 must vary by less than 2 cm; the authored rig measures 1.1 cm.
The same seed and the same dt sequence must reproduce the same pose exactly.

known_limits: Authored creative geometry and an authored gait; no anatomical or biomechanical claim is made, and the figure is nobody in particular.
The poly budget is the triangle count observed at default parameters.

The planted boot is not perfectly still: the hips counter-rotate 3 degrees per stride and the leg solve is sagittal only, so a stance boot drifts up to 1.1 cm in a straight line, measured over 240 frames at the default gait. A turn adds the arc the body walks. The quadruped, whose hips do not rotate, drifts 0.0 mm.
Rigid parts on rotating joints, no skinning and no cloth: the tunic does not react to the walk.

far.png, mid.png, close.png and detail.png are single frames of the delivered mid-stride pose; close-motion.png is the same view after kit-proof.py --motion-check advances animate(dt) by a fixed number of 1/60 s steps, so the walk cycle is proved by two frames, not by a film.

A 1.75 m figure does not quite fit the harness's close frame - at 0.78 of the fitting distance the vertical field is 1.61 m against a 1.71 m mid-stride bounding box - so close.png crops the top of the hat; far.png and mid.png carry the whole silhouette and detail.png carries the face.
create() returns the rig posed mid-stride rather than in its rest pose, so a single still reads as walking; the socket positions are still read off the rest pose, so they do not move with phase.

T2 is the same geometry with runtime procedural surface and vertex occlusion (see knowledge.surface-tier-defaults); it adds no polygons and ships no files, and it reads at stylized-game quality, not photoreal.
creative_affordances: Push scale to 0.7 for a child; the stride and the arm swing scale with it.
Swap tunic and re-seed for a crowd that shares a silhouette without repeating.
Raise strideHz above 1.6 and the same rig reads as a hurried walk, without a second clip.

defaults.rationale: A 0.72 m stride at 0.95 Hz is 0.68 m/s, the same cruise as the quadruped, so the two walk together on one lane; 0.6 duty keeps a moment of double support in every cycle, which is what separates a walk from a run.

T0.note: Bevelled box from the proof log bounds; the standing pose, not the stride envelope.

T2.note: Tunic, trousers, hood, belt, boots, soles and stitch beads take fabric (leather is read as fabric here; there is no leather family) and the buckle takes metal. Left flat on purpose: skin #d9a97f, eye #221c18 and the eye spark #fff6e6.

T3.note: No baked glTF ships for this blueprint: phase 9C baked only the two heroes (timber-cottage and watermill).

T4.note: No external asset ships with this skill.
